descripcion: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode. Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input. This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Vector CVSS:4.0 CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X Gravedad 4.0 6.90 Gravedad 4.0 txt MEDIUM Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) Pendiente de análisis

The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Vector CVSS:3.1 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) 8.00 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) HIGH

The NextScripts: Social Networks Auto-Poster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'comment_author' and 'comment_agent' Comment Fields in all versions up to, and including, 4.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the WordPress comment moderation queue, including pending and unapproved comments, meaning no prior approval of the comment is required for exploitation. 19/11/2026 19/11/2026 Vector CVSS:3.1 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) 7.20 Gravedad 3.1 Txt Gravedad 3.1 (CVSS 3.1 Base Score) HIGH
